acceptance_criteria.criterion: composer build in the framework produces correct modules-overview.md and module-glossary.md
composer build-dev in the HCP Editor produces correct modules-overview.md, module-glossary.md, and modules.json
Generated files show no content regressions compared to pre-change versions

summary: Both builds run cleanly and all three output files are correct.
Framework `composer build`: `modules-overview.md` (23 modules, 1 new) and `module-glossary.md` (timestamp only) — no content regressions.
HCP Editor `composer build-dev`: `modules-overview.md` (42 modules, 6 new framework modules) and `module-glossary.md` (69 new entries for 6 new modules) — all additive changes, no regression.

HCP Editor `composer generate-module-json`: `modules.json` generated with 14 modules (default brief-only mode) and `glossarySections: 1` (new TenantListProvider functionality working correctly for the first time).
`composer generate-module-json --all` verified: all 42 modules present including all pre-existing modules.
Regression tests: 76 Composer-module tests pass in framework; 11 HCP Editor tests pass; full framework suite 1005 pass / 7 fail (all LDAP config-file pre-existing failures unrelated to this plan).
New `ModuleJsonExportGenerator` framework base class confirmed working; thin HCP Editor subclass correctly overrides `resolveModuleSource()`.

comments.note: AC2 wording says 'composer build-dev produces modules.json', but modules.json is generated by the separate `composer generate-module-json` command. The AC is satisfied in spirit (the new generator works correctly), but the WP wording is imprecise. No action required.

In DEV mode, framework module source paths in modules-overview.md appear as absolute filesystem paths (e.g. `Users/smordziol/Webserver/...`) instead of relative `vendor/mistralys/...` paths. Root cause: ModuleContextFileFinder::normalizePath() calls realpath(), resolving the symlink used in DEV setup. This pre-existed before this plan — the old ModulesOverviewGenerator::resolveSourcePath() was identical code. PROD builds produce the correct relative paths. No regression; not introduced by this plan.

glossarySections now correctly populated in modules.json with TenantListProvider data (1 section, 5 entries via DecorateGlossaryEvent). This is new functionality per the plan and is working as designed.

summary: Integration code review PASS. Reviewed all 5 planned changes (A-E) spanning WP-001 through WP-007 as a unified whole. Architecture is sound: ModuleInfoParser uses BuildMessages throughout, KeywordGlossaryGenerator delegates to ModuleInfoParser and KeywordGlossaryBuilder, ReadmeOverviewParser moved to framework, dead collectGlossarySections() removed from HCP Editor, framework ModuleJsonExportGenerator created with correct Template Method hook design, HCP Editor reduced to a clean ~35-line thin subclass. No blocking issues found across all Review Dimensions.
Fix-Forward applied: added `final` to ReadmeOverviewParser — non-behavioral, consistent with neighboring ModuleInfoParser (pure static-method utility, no subclassing intent), verified by 7/7 tests.
Three carry-forward debt items from prior WP reviews remain open (missing unit tests, echo vs $onProgress inconsistency) — all previously documented and not blocking.

comments.note: Added `final` modifier to ReadmeOverviewParser. Non-behavioral change: the class has only static methods and no existing subclasses. Flagged by the WP-002 Reviewer but deferred because the Documentation agent owns documentation, not code. Applied here as a Fix-Forward to match the `final` convention established by the neighboring ModuleInfoParser. 7/7 ReadmeOverviewParser tests pass.

[documentation-forward] Three missing unit-test items remain open from prior WP reviews: (1) KeywordGlossaryBuilder has no dedicated test — conflict-warning path is untested (WP-005 QA); (2) framework ModuleJsonExportGenerator has no test covering generate(), $includeAll behaviour, or hook overrides (WP-006 QA + Reviewer); (3) HCP Editor resolveModuleSource() is covered only end-to-end via CLI, not by a focused unit test (WP-007 Reviewer). The Documentation agent should consolidate these into a single actionable recommendation in the module README so they are tracked as a follow-up.

ModuleJsonExportGenerator::generate() in the framework contains 4 direct echo calls (progress output) while KeywordGlossaryGenerator uses an optional $onProgress callable — creating an inconsistency within the same module. This was intentionally deferred in the plan (noted as WP-006 implementation comment). A follow-up should migrate the generator to the $onProgress pattern for consistency.

Hard-coded 'ModuleInfoParser' source label appears three times in ModuleInfoParser::parseFile() (WP-001 Reviewer observation, still open). A private const SOURCE = 'ModuleInfoParser' would eliminate the duplication and make a future rename a single-point change. Not blocking — the class is final and the string is stable.

Overall implementation quality is high. The five planned changes were executed in the correct dependency order, each WP was tightly scoped, and the resulting architecture correctly eliminates the identified duplications. The KeywordGlossaryBuilder extraction and the ModuleJsonExportGenerator Template Method design are exemplary patterns for this codebase.

notes: All three ACs verified as met via build execution and diff analysis. No code defects found.
All 152 tested assertions pass across framework and HCP Editor relevant test classes.

Notable improvements shipped: glossarySections now appears in modules.json for the first time (TenantListProvider via DecorateGlossaryEvent); 6 new framework modules (ai, api, api-cache, api-clients, api-openapi, api-parameters) now appear in HCP Editor generated docs.
Pre-existing LDAP test failures (7) are environment-config issues unrelated to this plan — they should not block code review.

Code review PASS. Fix-Forward applied: ReadmeOverviewParser is now final. Three carry-forward documentation items remain open (missing unit tests for KeywordGlossaryBuilder, framework ModuleJsonExportGenerator, and HCP Editor resolveModuleSource() — all flagged in prior WP reviews). No blocking issues. Plan objectives fully met across WP-001 through WP-007.
